[LSER.9.3.1a] **Default vs `realtime` divergence (cross-mode replay).**
The eviction above is the *default* backend's behaviour. Under
`realtime` / `linear_scan: false` the row map is locked at `go_live` and
backings are pre-allocated, so a sliding/tumbling backing is **never
evicted** — its state persists across a silence gap instead of
cold-starting. The two modes therefore compute **different series
values from the same event trace** after any window of silence: the
default backend re-warms from empty (warm-up-biased), while
`realtime` carries the pre-gap state forward. This is permitted —
the dialect is part of the compiled rule set, so it is a different
input under [LDET.1.1] — but it is a cross-mode **replay trap**: a
`realtime` production recording replayed on a default-built engine
(or vice versa) diverges on series-derived facts, so replay on a
build of the same dialect. The three signal aggregations do not diverge:
no mode evicts their state ([LSER.9.3.1], [LSIG.5.4]).
